text: BM25 is a probabilistic ranking function used in information retrieval. It is based on the Okapi BM25 formula and considers term frequency and inverse document frequency.
Dense retrieval uses neural embedding models to encode queries and documents into dense vector representations. Similarity is computed using cosine similarity or inner product.
Information retrieval evaluation metrics include NDCG, MRR, MAP, and Recall. These metrics measure how well a retrieval system ranks relevant documents.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) is a hybrid search technique that combines rankings from multiple retrieval systems. Each document receives a score based on its rank in each list.
NDCG stands for Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain. It measures retrieval quality by considering graded relevance and the position of relevant documents in the ranking.
TF-IDF is a classical text weighting scheme used in information retrieval. It combines term frequency with inverse document frequency to score term importance.
Cross encoders are neural models that jointly encode a query and document to produce a relevance score. They are more accurate than bi-encoders but slower.
ColBERT is a late-interaction retrieval model that encodes queries and documents into multi-vector representations and scores using MaxSim over token embeddings.
Precision and recall are classic retrieval metrics. Precision measures how many retrieved documents are relevant, while recall measures how many relevant documents are retrieved.
Hybrid retrieval combines sparse and dense retrieval signals. Common fusion methods include RRF, weighted sum, and learned fusion using a neural reranker.
